patch_description:
The previous implementation failed validation because it could corrupt row identity and cell placement during recursive processing. In particular, `column_recursion` wrote completed futures back using `result_df.loc[i]`, where `i` was completion order rather than the source row index. It also mixed reordered rows, reset indexes, merged temporary `original_index` columns, and finally sorted values independently of the returned column-order metadata. This could duplicate, misalign, or alter logical cells.

The replacement keeps every source row and cell exactly once, never adds helper columns to the returned data, and returns valid per-row column orderings. It builds a small bounded set of candidate field orders, scores candidates using the actual serialized-row Trie objective (lexicographic adjacent LCP), and selects the best candidate. It supports mixed values and missing values using the same empty-string normalization used by scoring, honors dependency and merge adjacency constraints with a safe global ordering fallback, and uses a bounded conditional grouping strategy when row-specific orders are allowed.
